parties.ourParty: The Deerskin Companies, Inc. (Company — customer/licensee of HDI's site development and hosting services)

plans.note: No liability-cap heading appears in the supplied outline; hosting/development agreements of this vintage often omit a cap or bury one in a general terms block near the signature page (sec-p0072). Sweep the unindexed body for 'liability', 'consequential', 'in no event' before concluding it is missing.

No indemnity section surfaced. Check the general/miscellaneous paragraphs preceding sec-p0072 for HDI indemnification of the Company for third-party IP and misconduct claims arising from the site build and hosting; if truly absent, flag as missing.

Nothing in the outline restricts the Company's businesses or sourcing. Because 'Deerskin Products' is a defined term, scan the commercial paragraphs for any covenant limiting where the Company may sell or source those products; only flag if a restriction actually binds us.

A site development and hosting deal tied to 'Deerskin Products' plausibly obliges the Company to use HDI as sole developer/host. sec-1.4 (HDI providing the Company access) is the nearest indexed anchor; look for 'sole', 'exclusive', 'shall not engage' language in the services paragraphs.
No pricing or most-favoured-customer language in the outline. Only actionable if a clause obliges the Company to extend HDI its best terms; an MFN running in our favour is not flagged.

sec-5.4 (each party appoints a representative/coordinator) puts named personnel in contact, which is where a reciprocal no-hire sometimes sits; otherwise no non-solicit appears. Flag only a restriction binding the Company that lacks a duration limit or general-advertising carve-out.

The defined term 'Termination Date' confirms termination machinery exists even though no termination heading is indexed. Locate it and test whether the Company may exit on notice without penalty and whether HDI has a broader mid-term walk-away right; 'Time of Receipt' likely governs when notice bites.

No term/renewal heading in the outline; check the paragraphs around the 'Termination Date' definition for an evergreen roll-over and the length of the non-renewal notice window before treating this as missing.

Governing law and venue almost always sit in the boilerplate immediately preceding the execution block at sec-p0072. Both parties are US corporations, so New York or Delaware is the expected (and acceptable) choice; note rather than flag an accepted-but-not-preferred state.

Assignment/successors language should appear in the boilerplate run leading into sec-p0072. Confirm the Company may assign to affiliates and successors and that HDI cannot terminate on our change of control — relevant given the affiliated-group posture of these parties.

sec-1.4 grants the Company access to HDI-side systems/materials and is the closest indexed hook for ownership questions. Verify the Company owns the site deliverables it pays for, its customer data and 'Deerskin Products' content, with no assignment of Company IP to HDI.

sec-1.4 ('HDI shall provide the Company with access to...') is the operative access/licence grant. Check it covers our affiliates and contractors and is not revocable at HDI's discretion; a bare access right with no stated scope should be read against the fallback before flagging.

No audit or records-inspection heading in the outline. If an audit right over the Company appears in the fees/reporting paragraphs, test notice, frequency, off-site conduct and who bears cost; audit rights running in our favour are not flagged.

No liquidated damages or penalty language surfaced. Only a stipulated sum payable by the Company (e.g., an early-termination or shortfall payment near the 'Termination Date' provisions) would trigger this rule; service credits owed to us are welcome.

No warranty heading is indexed; service-performance obligations may instead be embedded in the development/hosting paragraphs near sec-1.4 and the project-management arrangement in sec-5.4. Look also for an 'AS IS'/disclaimer sentence, which would be the deviation to address.

No insurance provision appears. HDI hosts the site and handles Company/customer data, so standard coverage (commercial general liability, tech E&O/cyber) is expected; treat as missing if no such paragraph exists in the unindexed body.

No fees or volume-commitment heading in the outline. Review the compensation paragraphs for any minimum spend, guaranteed hosting volume or take-or-pay tied to 'Deerskin Products'; flag only if there is no exit.

No wind-down heading surfaced, but the 'Termination Date' definition means there is a termination cluster to check for return of Company data, site content and domain/customer files plus migration help. If the termination paragraphs are silent, record as missing.
